body:
## Resolution
Category: correctness. Area: manage.sh (`require_running_container`, `run_lgsm`, `run_lgsm_noninteractive`, `show_status_one`, `show_logs`, `open_shell`, `exec_in_container`). Every command routed through `for_target()` calls its callback as `"$callback" "$service" "$@" || failed=1`. Per documented bash semantics, a shell function invoked as the tested command of an `||` list has `set -e` ignored for every command it executes, transitively. The 7 internal `id=$(require_container ...)` / `id=$(require_running_container ...)` assignments were unguarded, so when `die()` fired (only exiting its own command-substitution subshell) the failure was silently discarded and execution continued with an empty `id`, ultimately reaching `docker exec`/`docker inspect` with an empty container ID. Reproduced with a mock `docker` binary: `restart all` with Valheim's container missing printed both correct diagnostics, then a misleading "proceeding" log line (`./vhserver restart ()`), then a raw `Error: No such container:` from the exec call — the script's own guard clauses did not stop it; only Docker's own input validation did.
Fix applied: added `|| return 1` after each of the 7 unguarded lookups (explicit `return` is not subject to the `-e` exemption). Re-verified: `restart all` with Valheim missing now prints exactly one clean diagnostic for Valheim and correctly continues to restart the remaining servers (exit code 1, correctly reflecting the partial failure); `restart valheim` alone now stops cleanly after exactly one diagnostic.

Migrated from v1 `nitpicker-findings.md` (Pass 1, 2026-07-30).
title: `die()` does not abort bulk/per-target operations; script silently proceeds with an empty container ID

body:
## Resolution
Category: conventions. Area: manage.sh (`DISPLAY_NAMES`, `DEFAULT_SCRIPTS`). shellcheck 0.11.0 does not parse keys in a `readonly -A NAME=(...)` literal as associative-array string keys the way it does for `declare -A`, instead treating hyphenated keys as arithmetic subtraction of bare words, producing 8 SC2154 warnings. Confirmed via isolated repro that splitting into `declare -A NAME=(...)` + separate `readonly NAME` eliminates all warnings with identical runtime behavior.
Fix applied: replaced both `readonly -A NAME=(...)` declarations with `declare -A NAME=(...)` followed by `readonly NAME`. `shellcheck manage.sh` now exits 0 with no warnings.

Migrated from v1 `nitpicker-findings.md` (Pass 1, 2026-07-30).
title: `readonly -A` associative-array declarations trigger 8 shellcheck SC2154 false positives

## Resolution
Category: maintainability. Area: manage.sh (`interactive_menu`). The `select action in ...` list omitted `check-update`, `force-update`, `update-lgsm`, `validate`, `monitor`, `exec`, `upgrade`, and `help`, all valid top-level commands per `usage()` and the README's "Commands" table. Initially filed as Advisory (assumed intentional curation); user confirmed the omission was not intentional.
Fix applied: added all 8 missing commands to the menu's action list. `exec` needed extra handling since it requires a freeform command the `select` menu can't gather directly — the menu now prompts "Command to run:" and warns/re-prompts if left empty instead of silently failing later. `help` now shares the no-server-needed path with `list`/`doctor`. Verified via scripted stdin: selecting `exec` → a server → a command correctly invokes `docker exec -it --user linuxgsm <id> <command>`; selecting `help` prints `usage()` without prompting for a server.

Migrated from v1 `nitpicker-findings.md` (Pass 1, 2026-07-30).
title: Interactive menu exposes a subset of the documented CLI commands

body:
## Problem

`upgrade_one()` calls `run_lgsm_noninteractive "$service" update-lgsm`, then `update`, then `validate` as three unguarded sequential statements with no `||`/return-status check between them. `upgrade_one` is invoked as `"$callback" "$service" "$@" || failed=1` inside `for_target()` (same pattern documented in the now-fixed finding for require_container/require_running_container): a shell function called as the tested command of an `||` list has `-e` ignored for everything it executes, so a failing first or second step does not stop the third from running.

## Evidence

Reproduced with a mock `docker` binary: `./manage.sh upgrade valheim` with Valheim's container missing prints the identical diagnostic three times —
```
[ERR ] No Coolify-managed container found for 'valheim'. Deploy docker-compose.yaml first.
[ERR ] No Coolify-managed container found for 'valheim'. Deploy docker-compose.yaml first.
[ERR ] No Coolify-managed container found for 'valheim'. Deploy docker-compose.yaml first.
```
(exit=1). The now-fixed `require_running_container` guard stops each individual `run_lgsm_noninteractive` call cleanly, but `upgrade_one` itself has no equivalent guard between its three steps, so all three run and each independently hits and reports the same failure.

## Impact

Cosmetic in the missing-container case (tripled, redundant diagnostic instead of one). More significant when the container is running but `update-lgsm` fails for a real reason (network error, upstream LinuxGSM issue): `upgrade_one` proceeds to run `update` and then `validate` against a LinuxGSM installation that may be in a partially-updated, inconsistent state from the failed `update-lgsm` step, contradicting the documented sequential dependency ("`upgrade` runs these LinuxGSM operations sequentially") and risking a misleading "validate: OK" result over broken state.

## Fix

Add `|| return 1` after each of the three calls in `upgrade_one`:
```bash
upgrade_one() {
  local service=$1
  run_lgsm_noninteractive "$service" update-lgsm || return 1
  run_lgsm_noninteractive "$service" update || return 1
  run_lgsm_noninteractive "$service" validate || return 1
}
```

## Resolution
Added `|| return 1` after each of the 3 sequential calls in upgrade_one(). Verified: bats regression test "upgrade stops after the first failed step instead of repeating the diagnostic" fails on the pre-fix code (diagnostic printed 3x) and passes post-fix (printed once); "upgrade all skips the missing service but still upgrades the rest" confirms the remaining targets still complete.
title: upgrade_one() doesn't stop after a failed step, so update/validate run even after update-lgsm fails

body:
## Problem

All four services reference `ghcr.io/gameservermanagers/gameserver:<shortname>` (`:mc`, `:pz`, `:vh`, `:sdtd`) by mutable tag. The upstream image's own README states "This container image builds weekly," meaning the content behind each tag changes on a schedule without a corresponding version bump in this repo.

## Evidence

docker-compose.yaml lines 3, 19, 35, 51 all use bare `:<shortname>` tags with no digest. Confirmed via the upstream `GameServerManagers/docker-gameserver` README that the image "builds weekly."

## Impact

Every redeploy (Coolify re-pull, host reboot that re-pulls, etc.) can silently pull a different image build than the last deploy. A breaking change in a weekly upstream build affects all four servers simultaneously with no way to correlate the break to a repo change, and there is no way to redeploy an exact previously-known-good image state.

## Fix

Pin each image to a digest (`image: ghcr.io/gameservermanagers/gameserver:mc@sha256:...`) and update the digest deliberately (e.g. via a periodic manual bump or a Renovate/Dependabot digest-update rule), or at minimum document in README that redeploys are not reproducible and how to roll back to a prior digest via the registry.

## Resolution
Resolved each tag's current manifest digest from the GHCR registry API (anonymous pull token + Docker-Content-Digest header) and pinned all 4 images to tag@digest. Verified all 4 digests are well-formed (64 hex chars) and that `docker compose config` resolves each image reference to the exact intended string with no inserted whitespace. Wrapped the resulting long lines using YAML double-quoted backslash line-continuation (verified via `docker compose config` that this introduces zero extra characters) to keep yamllint's line-length rule clean.
title: Game server images are pinned to floating tags, not digests, for images that build weekly

body:
## Problem

manage.sh is a 440-line bash script with meaningful branching logic (command dispatch, per-target iteration, container lookup with multiple failure modes) and zero automated tests. There is no bats/shunit2 harness, and nothing exercises the failure paths (missing container, stopped container, multi-step command sequences).

## Evidence

`find . -type f` shows no `*.bats`, `test/`, or `tests/` directory. This exact untested surface already harbored two confirmed correctness bugs found this session purely by manual reasoning plus ad hoc mock-`docker` testing: the `for_target`/`die()` error-propagation bug (now fixed) and `upgrade_one()`'s un-guarded three-step sequence (filed separately) — both are exactly the class of bug a small scripted test with a stub `docker` binary would catch mechanically and keep catching on future changes.

## Impact

Regressions in the container-lookup/error-handling logic (the part of the script proven fragile) can be reintroduced silently by any future edit, with no automated signal before a real deployment surfaces it.

## Fix

Add a small `bats-core` (or `shunit2`) test suite under `test/` that stubs `docker` via `PATH` injection (the same technique used to verify this session's fixes) and covers: missing container, stopped container, and the multi-step `upgrade` sequence for both single-target and `all`.

## Resolution
Added test/manage.bats (bats-core), stubbing `docker` via PATH injection. 8 tests covering: missing-container error propagation (single-target and `all`), the upgrade-sequence short-circuit, `list`'s non-fatal missing-container reporting, and unknown-server/command rejection. Verified the suite is not tautological: the two regression-focused tests fail against a copy of the code with the NP-001/upgrade_one fixes reverted, and pass against the current fixed code.
title: No automated tests exist for manage.sh's command dispatch and error-propagation logic

body:
## Problem

`manage.sh monitor <server|all>` runs "LinuxGSM monitor check" (a process-responsiveness check LinuxGSM can use to detect and restart a hung-but-still-running game server), but nothing in the repository invokes it periodically. Docker's `restart: unless-stopped` policy only recovers a container that has actually exited; it cannot detect a game process that is alive but unresponsive.

## Evidence

`manage.sh` implements and documents `monitor` (usage text, README "Commands" table) but the repository contains no cron file, systemd timer, or Coolify scheduled-task config that calls it, and README's "Management" section only shows it as a manually-typed example command.

## Impact

A hung (not crashed) game server process is not auto-recovered — only a container restart, not a hung process, is covered by the existing restart policy. Recovery depends entirely on an operator remembering to run `./manage.sh monitor all` by hand.

## Fix

Document (or provide) a periodic invocation, e.g. a host crontab entry (`*/5 * * * * /path/to/manage.sh monitor all`) or a Coolify scheduled task, and mention it in README's "Management" section.

## Resolution
Added a crontab example and explanation to README.md's "Management" section, documenting why `monitor` needs external scheduling (Docker's restart policy only recovers exited containers, not hung-but-alive processes).
title: LinuxGSM's `monitor` self-healing command is implemented but never scheduled to run automatically

body:
## Problem

The repository has no `LICENSE` (or `LICENSE.md`/`COPYING`) file declaring the terms under which this code may be used, copied, or modified.

## Evidence

`find . -type f -not -path './.git/*'` lists `docker-compose.yaml`, `manage.sh`, `README.md`, `.env.example`, and `docs/audit/findings/*` — no license file anywhere.

## Impact

Without an explicit license, the default legal position in most jurisdictions (and GitHub's own stated policy) is that no one else has any right to use, copy, or modify the code, even if the repository itself is publicly visible. This is inconsistent with a repo polished enough to document deployment and management for other Coolify/LinuxGSM users.

## Fix

Add a `LICENSE` file with the owner's chosen license (e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0) and, if desired, reference it from README.md.

## Resolution
Added LICENSE (MIT, user's choice) and a short "License" section in README.md linking to it.
title: No LICENSE file in the repository
